entities.summary: Belesys (b. 400 BCE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in Global. He was a key figure in the administration of the city of Athens during the Peloponnesian War (431-404 BCE) and played a crucial role in the development of the Athenian navy. Belesys was known for his military prowess and his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the city-states of ancient Greece. He was a prominent figure in the Athenian government and was instrumental in the city's efforts to maintain its independence and resist the growing power of Sparta. Belesys's legacy can be seen in the many reforms he implemented during his tenure, including the establishment of a new system of taxation and the expansion of the Athenian navy. He died in 344 BCE, leaving behind a lasting impact on the city of Athens and the wider world of ancient Greece.
